name: Hebrew
about: Written right to left with 22 letters; everyday writing leaves out most vowels. We teach block print letters; everyday handwriting uses a different cursive style.

phrases.how: Right to left. ם is the special form of מ used only at the end of a word.
phrases.why: Greet someone in their own script on a card or a note.
phrases.dictation: Four letters, right to left: ש ל ו ם.

phrases.how: Most vowels aren't written: ו stands for the 'o' and the final ה for the 'a'.
phrases.why: Write a real thank-you card to a host or to family.
phrases.dictation: Four letters, right to left: ת ו ד ה.

phrases.how: Same letter, two shapes: the word starts with מ and ends with final ם.
phrases.why: Spot it on a menu, a sign or a bottle label.
phrases.dictation: Three letters, right to left: מ י ם.

phrases.how: ח is a throaty 'ch', like in Bach. The vowels a and e aren't written.
phrases.why: Sign a note to a friend. Writing it by hand helps you remember it.
phrases.dictation: Three letters, right to left: ח ב ר.

phrases.how: א often carries a vowel without a sound of its own; here it starts 'e-chad'.
phrases.why: Read quantities and order one of something off a menu.
phrases.dictation: Three letters, right to left: א ח ד.
